verdict.rationale: v0's own docs say a project can connect to GitHub to keep its code in a repository, work on isolated branches, run CI and publish through pull requests, and push code directly to the user's repo. Inbound flow is covered by Import from GitHub plus in-product Fix Conflicts and Fix CI actions on branches, which implies v0 reconciles with repository changes. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of continuous pulling of externally made commits back into a v0 chat, and independent or hands-on confirmation of round-trip sync.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync my project to my own GitHub repository and keep changes flowing both ways

citations.quote: Connect a v0 project to GitHub to keep its code in a repository, work on isolated branches, preview changes, run CI, and publish through pull requests.
Connect to GitHub and push code directly to your repository.
To start from code already on GitHub, use Import from GitHub. Importing creates a chat at the selected base branch
open the branch menu and select Fix Conflicts, Fix CI, or Fix CI + Conflicts.
